policies.summary: Separate discovery, planning, execution, and verification; never infer completion from execution alone.
Assign one canonical owner to every responsibility, contract, state, and generated artifact.
Classify risk before selecting approval, containment, testing, and rollback requirements.
Deny undeclared effects and require explicit authority for external or high-impact changes.
Bind material claims and completion decisions to current, typed, reproducible evidence.
Trace approved changes through scope, impact, tests, evidence, and rollback.
Checkpoint resumable work and recover from partial execution without repeating unsafe effects.
Certify only against the current discovery denominator and unresolved-risk record.
Keep execution inside approved effects, paths, budgets, and approval boundaries.
Keep external tools inert until provenance, integrity, permissions, license, and risk pass review.
Collect only opt-in, redacted assurance signals with bounded retention.
Preserve protected, evidentiary, external, and unknown data; reclaim only conclusively owned ephemerals after safety and retention gates.
Register and reconcile owned workspaces and process trees across completion, failure, cancellation, and recovery.
Route optional accelerators only with compatibility, VRAM, correctness, benchmark, telemetry, and fallback evidence.
Freeze benchmark treatments, protect cold runs, bound retries, and separate infrastructure failures from graded results.
Turn sealed evidence into independently admitted and verified improvement candidates without self-certification.
Separate Codex-host and PX governance boundaries while keeping native discovery and execution authority explicit.
Classify every release file as product input, evidence output, generated intermediate, or bounded control output before hashing and certification.
Require executed branch coverage and per-test contexts for safety-critical release classes.
Trust effect authority only when a scoped, unexpired grant has a verified publisher signature.
Verify signed release certificates against explicitly trusted and non-revoked publisher keys.
Admit only reviewed public identifiers, inert test domains, technical URI tokens, and binary signatures during sanitation review.
Bound Python and operating-system support claims to the public CI and release matrices.
Keep specialist routing bounded, lazy, project-scoped, evidence-governed, and separate from runtime authority.
PX governs admitted scope and evidence while each host retains its native execution, approval, and security authority.
Promote learned candidates only through hash-bound evidence, confidence, comparison, independent validation, measured reuse, and reversible lifecycle gates.
Recommend bounded execution placement only against the current baseline, full boundary cost, correctness, rollback, and after-state evidence.
Archive superseded PX-owned map and committed-WAL evidence only after bounded-path, member-hash, archive-integrity, and recovery-receipt gates.

loading_rule: Load a full policy body only when the request, selected capability, or declared effect references its policy ID.
